Tips & Articles

5 Tips to Make Your Motion Graphics Look Smoother

Smooth motion is the first thing viewers notice, even if they cannot explain why. The biggest secret is easing. Objects in real life do not start and stop at full speed, so use ease in and ease out on your movements. This one change makes animation feel natural.

Second, do not move everything at the same time. Let elements start a few frames apart so the eye can follow them. Third, keep your timing consistent across the whole video. Fourth, use a steady frame rate such as 30 or 60 frames per second and keep it the same from start to export. Finally, export with a good quality setting so the smooth motion is not damaged by heavy compression.

How to Edit Short Videos for Reels, TikTok and Shorts

Short videos win or lose in the first three seconds. Start with the most interesting moment or a clear question, and avoid slow intros. Use the vertical 9:16 size (1080 by 1920) so your video fills the whole phone screen.

Cut out silence and pauses to keep the pace fast. Add captions, because many people watch without sound. Keep important text away from the very top and bottom of the screen, where the app buttons and description cover it. Finish with a simple ending that makes people replay or follow.

CapCut, Filmora or Premiere Pro: Which One Should You Choose?

All three can make great videos, so the best choice depends on your needs. CapCut is free to start, quick to learn and has useful features like auto captions and ready-made effects. It is a good choice for short videos.

Filmora is friendly for beginners and has many built-in effects and titles. Premiere Pro is the professional option with a powerful timeline and more control, but it takes longer to learn and is paid. If you are just starting, begin with CapCut or Filmora, and move to Premiere Pro when you need more control.

Why Good Audio Matters in Video Editing

Viewers forgive a slightly imperfect picture, but they leave quickly when the sound is bad. Always make the voice clear first. Remove background noise where you can and keep the voice at a steady volume from start to end.

Keep music lower than the voice so people can understand every word. Use sound effects carefully, only to support an action or a transition, and not all the time. Before exporting, listen with headphones and also on a phone speaker, because most people will watch on a phone.
